title: Identifying devices of style and tone (1)

instruction.text: Find the right description for each device of style and tone.

atoms.b: an indirect reference to a person, place, event, etc.
an overused phrase that lost its originality due to excessive repetition
a statement that is intentionally overstated
the opposite of what is said
the outcome is the opposite of what is expected
the audience knows more than the characters
two contrasting ideas are placed side by side to highlight their differences
a question that is asked for effect rather than to get an actual answer
a statement that makes a situation seem less important, serious, or intense than it actually is
the manipulation of language for humorous effect

instruction.text: Choose which device of style and tone is being used.

atoms.a: When a character in a horror movie says “I'll be right back” and the audience already knows they won't survive.
Rich and poor, young and old, happy and sad – the concert attracted everyone.
The past, present, and future walked into a bar. It was tense.
It is way too expensive. Do you think money grows on trees?

“Fantastic! Just what I needed today!”

(The person who said this is clearly upset.)
I called you a thousand times yesterday.
